subject: POC Onramp checklist: model choices, fallback strategy, and evaluation metrics
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Emily Park <emily@lexishealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 18:05:00 -0700
Subject: POC onramp checklist: model choices, fallback strategy, and evaluation metrics

Hi Emily — thanks again for the call today. Wanted to capture the next steps and a proposed onramp so we can align expectations before we kick off the trial. I’ve noted owners for each item; please correct anything that’s off.

Summary / goals
- Scope: 2-week POC (30 days optional) to validate intent classification + extraction + multilingual support for EN/ES/FR in your support ticketing flow.
- Primary objective: achieve >=88% intent accuracy and <=500ms 90th percentile latency for short messages (<=256 tokens) on hosted Redwood API.
- Secondary: validate fallback behavior under capacity and whether a dedicated quantized model improves cost per 1k tokens by ~30%.

Model recommendation (proposed)
- Primary model: Llama-3-13B-instruct (8-bit quantized) — best balance for multilingual understanding and quality on extraction tasks.
- Fallback model: Mistral-Instruct-7B (int8) as a cheaper, lower-latency fallback for degraded capacity.
- For high-volume Spanish/French bursts: option to route to a small dedicated 13B pool or use on-the-fly translation + monolingual model depending on throughput.

Acceptance / success criteria (POC) — tracked in attached spreadsheet
- Intent classification: micro-F1 >= 0.88 on a 500-example holdout per locale.
- Extraction (entities): span F1 >= 0.84 averaged across locales.
- Latency: 90th percentile <= 500ms for hosted; if routed to Dedicated, 95th percentile <= 200ms.
- Cost target: average token cost <= $0.0035 per 1k tokens for inference (hosted baseline).
- Rollback / safety checks: no increase in hallucination rate > 3% on flagged prompts.

Evaluation plan & owners
- Lexis to provide: ~1,500 labeled prompts (mix of EN/ES/FR), plus 3 canonical failure examples (owner: Emily).
- Redwood solutions (Marissa): construct evaluation harness, produce daily quality reports, model-fallback simulation, and provide a baseline run within 48 hours of receiving data.
- Redwood sales (Ben): finalize PoC commercial terms and any NDAs / data access forms.
- Technical kickoff: target Wed 2026-09-16.

Kickoff timeline (proposed)
- 9/14: this recap + confirm owners and dataset delivery schedule (Emily)
- 9/16: kickoff call (engineering + data + procurement) — set final routes and rate limits
- 9/17–9/24: ingestion, baseline runs, and initial metrics
- 9/25–9/30: optimization (batching, quantization tweak, fallback tuning) and acceptance run

Asks for you this week
1) Confirm dataset delivery ETA (CSV / JSONL) and whether any data needs to remain in your VPC (if so, we’ll switch to Private onramp).
2) Confirm whether Spanish + French need native multilingual model vs translation flow (quick preference will guide model routing).
3) Any procurement constraints (POC purchase order or SOW) we should be aware of.

Attached: POC_Success_Criteria_v1.xlsx (live metric sheet) and a small test prompt set placeholder — please replace with your canonical examples.

Thanks — Laura

--

Laura — thanks, this looks thorough. A few clarifications from our side:  

1) Dataset: we can deliver the labeled sample by EOD Thu 9/17 as CSV + JSONL. Some PHI redaction is required; we will provide mapping notes.
2) Multilingual preference: we’d like to prioritize native multilingual model support for Spanish. French is lower volume and can tolerate translation for the POC.
3) Procurement: we need a short SOW and invoice (PO) before starting; procurement can turn that around in 3–5 business days.

On the models: curious whether Redwood has prior benchmarks comparing Llama-3-13B-instruct vs Mistral-Instruct-7B specifically for entity extraction on shorter customer support snippets? Latency budget is tight.

I’ll join the kickoff on 9/16.

—Emily

Hi Emily — quick note on procurement and cost framing before the kickoff:

- SOW/PO: we’ll produce a concise SOW that covers the 2-week baseline + optional 2-week extension; I’ll send a draft by EOD today so procurement has something to review.
- Pricing: hosted POC (usage + small setup fee): estimated $6k–$9k for the baseline (depends on token volumes and test runs). Dedicated pilot (if you want reserved GPUs for Spanish bursts) is an additional monthly minimum; we can discuss credits if you convert to a committed reserved plan after the POC.
- Benchmarks: Redwood has internal microbenchmarks comparing the two models on extraction for short form text: Llama-3-13B tends to be 6–12% better on entity F1 for these kinds of prompts at the cost of ~25% higher average tokens. Mistral-Instruct-7B is materially cheaper and ~30% lower latency on equivalent hardware. Marissa — can you paste the short benchmark summary in thread before kickoff?

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>

Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: POC onramp checklist: model choices, fallback strategy, and evaluation metrics

Emily — adding the solutions/ops perspective and the evaluation plan I’ll own. Quick paste of what we’ll run and how we’ll measure:  

Evaluation harness (owner: marissa_cole)
- Ingest lexis_test_prompts_v2 (split: 70/30 train/holdout; holdout must be untouched).
- Baseline runs: run both candidate models (Llama-3-13B-instruct and Mistral-Instruct-7B) against the holdout for EN/ES/FR where data exists.
- Metrics: intent micro-F1, entity span F1, token consumption, 90th P50/P95 latency, hallucination flags (heuristic + human review on 50 samples).
- A/B gating: acceptance requires primary model (Llama-3-13B-instruct) to exceed the thresholds in the attached spreadsheet; if not met but Mistral meets lower thresholds + cost target, we’ll propose fallback-as-primary for Spanish and discuss Dedicated options.

Operational tests
- Fallback simulation: synthetic capacity reduction (50% of requests dropped) to ensure fallback routing triggers and observe end-to-end error budget impact.
- Rate-limit behavior: ensure throttling is visible in traces and degrade gracefully to cached responses for repeated prompts.

Deliverables & timings
- 9/17: ingestion complete & baseline run (initial report)
- 9/20: mid-POC review (live dashboard + early metrics)
- 9/24: final acceptance run + handoff notes

Notes on multilingual approach
- For Spanish high-volume: two choices — native multilingual route (better quality, higher cost) or translation + monolingual prompt (lower cost, small quality delta). We’ll show delta in the 9/20 mid-review.

I’ve attached POC_Success_Criteria_v1.xlsx and the test prompt zip. If you can grant a temporary S3 link for the dataset, we’ll pull directly and start the baseline.

Thanks — Marissa
